extracted.intended_audience: State Exchanges, Federally-facilitated Exchange operators, health insurance issuers, agents, brokers, web-brokers, and compliance officers
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and procedural requirements for Exchanges, agents/brokers/web-brokers, and issuers regarding marketing, enrollment, documentation, URRT reporting, direct enrollment, eligibility determinations, and failure-to-file-and-reconcile policies under the proposed HHS/CMS rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to HHS investigations of misleading marketing
rubrics_metrics.description: Agents, brokers, and web-brokers investigated for misleading marketing must respond to HHS requests to provide confirmation they removed the ads and/or reviewed the marketing guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notifications to the agents, brokers, or web-brokers will detail required responses and provide hyperlinks to the noncompliant ad(s). HHS estimates one hour per response; HHS may request advertisements for review. Cost estimate example: $58.04 per response using an insurance sales agent wage rate.

rubrics_metrics.name: URRT CSR reporting and related Actuarial Memorandum requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Issuers must enter the actual amount of CSRs paid for enrollees (2 years prior), the amount of CSRs they expect to provide to enrollees, and a new field to gather the 'load amount' in the URRT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issuers incur ongoing burden to gather the three values and enter them into the URRT. Estimated annual burden examples: $572,118 (5,700 hours) to update/run standard methodology calculations; $429.47 (3.6 hours) to provide CSR related information in URRT; $1,718.27 (14.2 hours) to provide CSR calculation explanations in the Actuarial Memorandum. Estimated initial one-time cost to develop claim-level re-adjudication process using standard methodology (§156.430) provided (example figures for small issuers). See referenced sections for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: HHS authority to audit or conduct compliance reviews related to APTC/CSR/user fee programs
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS may audit or conduct compliance reviews to assess issuers' compliance with requirements related to APTC, CSR, and user fee programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS expects such audits would not impose additional costs beyond existing audit review processes. Example burden: business operations specialist 10 hours ($44.41/hr) to compile/submit data; compliance officer 4 hours ($40.86/hr) to review/sign off; estimated cost per issuer ≈ $607.54. Total cost contingent on number of small issuers selected for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: State Exchange Blueprint submission and public engagement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A State submitting an Exchange Blueprint application to operate a State Exchange must submit at least 15 months prior to proposed open enrollment start date and must conduct public engagements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon submission, the State must issue public notice including copy of Blueprint, Plan Year description, and information about public engagements. State must conduct at least one public engagement (in-person or virtual) effective in timeline/manner and provide opportunities for input, and conduct periodic public engagements thereafter until HHS approves or conditionally approves.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-required benefits treated as 'in addition to EHB'
rubrics_metrics.description: A State may require a QHP to cover benefits in addition to essential health benefits only if the State-required benefits meet all listed criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The four criteria for benefits to be considered 'in addition to EHB' are: (i) required by a State action taking place after December 31, 2011; (ii) applicable to the small group and/or individual markets; (iii) specific to required care, treatment, or services; and (iv) not required by State action for purposes of compliance with Federal requirements. A State must make payments to defray the cost of any such State-required benefits in accordance with paragraph (b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer assistance tools: non-Exchange web-broker eligibility application interface
rubrics_metrics.description: Exchanges must allow, as an alternative, non-Exchange web-broker entities to implement consumer websites that allow submission of the approved single streamlined eligibility application, provided they interface with the State Exchange.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-Exchange web-broker websites must transmit eligibility application information to the State Exchange so the Exchange may make eligibility determinations and communicate determinations to applicants. For State-based Exchanges on the Federal platform, directs individuals to submit through the Federal eligibility and enrollment platform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer selection/enrollment via non-Exchange web-brokers and recordkeeping interface
rubrics_metrics.description: State Exchanges may allow non-Exchange web-brokers to provide consumer websites that allow selection and enrollment in QHPs, provided they interface with the State Exchange to transmit plan selection and enrollment information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures the State Exchange can maintain records of all enrollments and meet other requirements under subpart E. If State-based Exchange on Federal platform, directs consumers to use the Federal platform for selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of conduct for agents, brokers, and web-brokers
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals or entities assisting enrollment must provide consumers with correct information without omission of material fact and refrain from conduct that is misleading, coercive, or discriminatory (race, color, national origin, disability, age, sex).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes refraining from conduct such as having a direct enrollment website that could mislead consumers into believing they are visiting HealthCare.gov. Agents/brokers/web-brokers must comply with §155.220(j)(2) standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation that eligibility application information has been reviewed and confirmed by the consumer
rubrics_metrics.description: Documenting that eligibility application information has been reviewed and confirmed by the consumer or their authorized representative must be effectuated by having the consumer take an action to execute the HHS-approved consumer consent form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The action taken must be clear on the face of the documentation (examples: hand-written or electronic written signature or initials, an email from the consumer, a recorded verbal conversation, or other means). A signature that is simply typed on the documentation or a filled-in check box does not clearly indicate review/confirmation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation that consent was provided by the consumer
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtaining and documenting the receipt of consent is effectuated by having the consumer or their authorized representative take an action to execute the HHS-approved consumer consent form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The action must be clear on the face of the documentation (hand-written/electronic signature or initials, an email, a recorded verbal conversation, etc.). A simply typed signature or a filled-in check box does not properly indicate consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marketing requirements for agents, brokers, and web-brokers
rubrics_metrics.description: Agents, brokers, and web-brokers assisting enrollment must provide correct information without omission and refrain from marketing that is misleading, materially inaccurate, coercive, or discriminatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement is in addition to standards of conduct; entities must comply with §155.220(j)(2) and (j)(3)(ii)-(iii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of prohibited misleading marketing practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific illustrative practices that are prohibited in marketing FFE plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include but are not limited to: (A) providing cash, monetary rebates, gift cards, travel vouchers, or cash equivalents as an inducement for enrollment; (B) offering gifts unless nominal value, offered to similarly situated consumers regardless of enrollment, and not cash/cash equivalents; (C) falsely asserting consumers will always qualify for zero-dollar insurance/zero-dollar premiums; (D) falsely using identical or facsimiles of government/official logos and notations; (E) miscommunicating enrollment timelines/deadlines; (F) misconstruing legislation/regulations/Executive Orders, including listing fake or incorrect references/citations; (G) utilizing image/likeness or quote from notable figure claiming endorsement when not truthful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production and availability of marketing materials upon HHS request
rubrics_metrics.description: Agents, brokers, and web-brokers must produce any marketing material upon request within the timeframe HHS mandates for monitoring, audit, and enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An entity is responsible to ensure all marketing-related materials created by or on their behalf adhere to marketing requirements and must make all such materials available upon request consistent with §155.220(j)(3)(iv) and (v).

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct Enrollment Option approval criteria for State Exchanges
rubrics_metrics.description: A State may elect to use one or more web-brokers to provide non-Exchange online enrollment that constitutes enrollment through the Exchange, subject to HHS approval and specified conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions for HHS approval include: (1) demonstrating operational readiness to enroll qualified individuals via approved direct enrollment websites including eligibility determinations and APTC/CSR handling; (2) providing an implementation plan and timeline with key activities, milestones, and communication/outreach strategy; (3) demonstrating at least one direct enrollment entity meets minimum Federal requirements (§§155.220 and 155.221), displays detailed QHP information, meets accessibility requirements (§155.205(c)), and is capable of enrolling all consumers including complex cases. If no entity meets requirements, the State Exchange must offer its consumer-facing website as soon as practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Options for conducting eligibility determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Exchanges may conduct eligibility determinations directly (Exchange carries out all determinations) or, for State-based Exchanges on the Federal platform, through a Federal platform agreement where HHS carries out determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This defines permissible operational approaches for handling eligibility determinations under §155.302.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision to eligibility standards: inclusion of 'eligible noncitizen'
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant must be a U.S. citizen, U.S. national, or an eligible noncitizen as defined in §155.20.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed addition defines eligible noncitizen by reference to 26 U.S.C. 36B(e)(2)(B) and adds 'Eligible noncitizen' to §155.20 definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to file and reconcile (FTR) policy for APTC eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: For plan year 2027, Exchanges must implement either a 1-tax-year FTR policy or a 2-tax-year FTR policy for determining APTC eligibility; for plan year 2028 and beyond, Exchanges must implement a 1-tax-year FTR policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exchanges must apply any chosen policy uniformly to all tax filers (and spouses if married). Definitions: failing to file and reconcile for 1 tax year occurs when HHS notifies the Exchange that APTC payments were made for the most recent year and the tax filer/spouse did not file and reconcile per 26 U.S.C. 6011/6012 and 26 CFR. Failing for 2 tax years is defined analogously for two most recent consecutive years. See paragraph (f)(4)(ii) for precise IRS-notification-based definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice requirements for Exchanges implementing FTR policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific notice obligations apply depending on whether an Exchange implements a 1-tax-year or 2-tax-year FTR policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If implementing a 2-tax-year policy, for tax filers failing for 1 year the Exchange must either: (i) send a notification to the tax filer (consistent with Federal Tax Information protection) informing them of the determination and educating them to file and reconcile to avoid future ineligibility; or (ii) send a notification to the tax filer or enrollee that they may be at risk of future ineligibility, educating on filing/reconciliation while not directly stating IRS indicates failure. For tax filers failing for 2 consecutive years, the Exchange must either: (i) send direct notification explicitly informing the tax filer of failure to file and reconcile and the risk of ineligibility after two years; or (ii) send an indirect notification to the tax filer or enrollee that they may be at risk of ineligibility after two years, educating them without directly stating IRS indicates failure. If implementing a 1-tax-year policy, the Exchange must either: (1) send a notification to the tax filer informing them of the determination and need to file/reconcile and risk of immediate ineligibility; or (2) send a notification to the tax filer or their enrollee informing they may be at risk, educating on the requirement without directly stating IRS indicates failure.
